verifiedPublicFacts.claim: CANO homepage leads with authority-insider positioning: Eduardo Cano states he worked inside the authority and directed fiscal-crime investigations.
CANO states 20 years exclusively in criminal law and describes experience beginning in 2006 in Delitos Fiscales y Financieros at the Procuraduría Fiscal de la Federación.
CANO already publishes a dedicated Delitos fiscales y financieros practice page; a new generic duplicate landing is therefore not assumed necessary.

The fiscal practice page explicitly addresses auditorías, requerimientos, SAT/UIF/Fiscalía information crossings, defraudación fiscal, nonexistent operations, contraband, money laundering, legal representatives and accountants.
CANO publicly offers Diagnóstico y estrategia for MXN 2,500.
The homepage already separates citatorio, detenido and víctima pathways and routes them toward contact/WhatsApp.
CANO publishes a fiscal-defense case involving a company owner accused of tax fraud and an asserted accounting-fraud finding by the defense.
CANO publishes a WTC Ciudad de México office address and contact channels.

userSuppliedAuditClaims.claim: Generic abogado penalista CDMX search demand is saturated and often contaminated by Fiscalía/Ministerio Público intent.
Penal-fiscal direct-response/local acquisition appears substantially less developed than generic criminal-defense acquisition.
The intersection of deep fiscal/accounting knowledge and adversarial criminal-procedure experience is structurally uncommon.
A reported five-year CDMX figure of 415 people denounced for SAT evasion was identified; this figure requires primary-source reconciliation before commercial use.
An interactive fiscal calendar could attract business owners and accountants before a matter escalates into criminal exposure.
Recent CDMX enforcement data indicate falling high-impact crime incidence can coexist with rising judicializations and arrest warrants.
Private-market reference ranges cited by the audit include higher-ticket full criminal litigation than CANO's MXN 2,500 diagnostic entry point.
Competitors commonly repeat 24-hour, accusatory-system and free-advice messaging, leaving authority-insider differentiation underused.

marketCorrections.claim: Penal-fiscal legal competition in CDMX is not empty; specialized firms exist. The narrower hypothesis is underdevelopment of local/direct-response acquisition.
Interactive fiscal calendars already exist in Mexico; differentiation cannot be the calendar alone.
The 415-person figure contains an apparent inconsistency in a secondary report and is not accepted as a hard market-size input.
Published private fee ranges are market references, not an official representative price distribution.
No current CPC, search-volume or paid-SERP claim is accepted because the connected research source could not refresh those metrics in the current audit window.
